transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Aperture - Head of ML), Marcus Reed (Aperture - Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Aperture - CTO)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on SLO defs, measurement plan, and who provides what artifacts.

[00:00] Sara: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, I'm Sara, AE at Redwood, Diego's our SE, we'll run through how we suggest scoping the POC for latency/throughput SLOs.
[00:22] Lena: Hi! thanks. our main ask is to make sure chat latency feels snappy for users. we have a 5s threshold for first response in the UI but we want tighter p95 numbers.
[00:38] Diego: got it. just to align terminology up front: we'll use TTFT for time-to-first-token, and TPOT to mean steady-state per-token latency (sometimes called time-per-token). some folks also track total response time but for streaming use-cases TTFT + TPOT give you the best signal.
[01:05] Marcus: quick question — how do you handle warm vs cold starts? our traffic bursts in mornings and we care about p99 more than p95 because of SLAs to partners.
[01:18] Diego: yes, important. our plan is to separate measurements: cold-start (first request after idle), warm-start steady-state (after prefix/KV cache populated). we'll capture both and report p50/p95/p99.
[01:40] Priya: what's realistic here? we see average prompt lengths ~30 tokens and then models generate ~80 tokens on average.
[01:51] Diego: ok that's helpful. two axes to size: QPS (incoming requests/sec) and token/s throughput once the model is generating. for POC we usually run a 48-hour harness: synthetic traffic matching token lengths and concurrency to capture variance and tail metrics.
[02:12] Sara: customers often want target numbers. based on similar workloads, we propose starting targets: TTFT p95 < 300ms, TTFT p99 < 700ms for small chat prompts; TPOT p95 ~ 20-30ms/token for steady-state on our recommended dedicated config. we can tighten when we see the real prompt set.
[02:40] Lena: 300ms p95 sounds optimistic; are those numbers for hosted or dedicated?
[02:48] Diego: mostly for Dedicated with pinned capacity and optimized kernels; hosted can be similar but depends on burst isolation. for Dedicated we can hit lower TTFT because we keep warm KV caches and persistent sessions. hosted (multi-tenant) numbers might be 10-20% higher on tails.
[03:10] Marcus: can you explain TPOT a bit more with an example?
[03:16] Diego: sure — if a model emits 10 tokens, TPOT is the per-token latency once streaming starts. so total generate time approximates TTFT + tokens * TPOT. e.g., TTFT 200ms + 80 tokens * 25ms = ~2.2s end-to-end.
[03:37] Priya: that calc helps. our UI budget is 2.5s typical for full response, so we need to hit the TTFT+TPOT combo.
[03:45] Sara: perfect. so success criteria should be both TTFT p95/p99 thresholds and total response p95 for representative prompts. we recommend defining success as: TTFT p95 < 300ms, TTFT p99 < 700ms, TPOT p95 < 30ms, and end-to-end response p95 < 2.5s for the canonical prompt set. these are negotiable based on their corpus.
[04:12] Lena: ok we can try that. what about measurement artifacts — how do you ensure fairness across runs?
[04:20] Diego: plan: Redwood will run three benchmark types: 1) Cold-start spike test (idle->burst) 2) Warm steady-state 48-hour run to capture diurnal variance 3) Stress run to find saturation point and token throughput. we will instrument to report p50/p95/p99 TTFT and TPOT and also resource utilization (GPU, mem).
[04:47] Marcus: do you simulate prefixes / agent context? our models use fairly long convo histories.
[04:53] Diego: yes include representative prefixes; please provide a sample corpus with token length distribution. we also recommend 10% cache-miss requests to mimic real-world variability.
[05:10] Priya: what about measuring TPOT across different quantization/instance types?
[05:16] Diego: we'll include multiple model variants in the run — full fp16, int8/ltq variants we support — and note the latency/cost tradeoff. for throughput scaling we'll run both single-instance and multi-GPU configs to recommend Dedicated sizing.
[05:34] Lena: timeline expectations?
[05:38] Sara: proposed POC cadence: week 0 (kickoff + share artifacts), week 1 (Redwood config + initial small-run), week 2 (48h benchmark + analysis), week 3 (final tuning + recommendation). total 3 weeks to conclusive recommendation; we suggested a 2-4 week POC window.
[06:00] Marcus: who owns the benchmark harness? can we run it ourselves?
[06:05] Diego: Redwood will provide the harness and a reproducible config. we can give you the scripts (we use k6/locust + a model-driver). you can run locally or Redwood runs it against Dedicated capacity. we'll publish raw artifacts (CSV/JSON) and a short analysis doc.
[06:22] Lena: good. small note — our security team needs KMS and audit logs for Private deployments; will that affect latencies?
[06:30] Sara: generally KMS calls are async cached, negligible for per-token costs, but we should include end-to-end tests if you want Private. audit logs don't typically add per-request latency but will affect throughput if logs are sync-blocking; we can configure async buffers.
[06:52] Priya: on success criteria we also need cost thresholds — e.g., max $ per 1M tokens during POC.
[06:58] Sara: we can include cost-per-token estimates in the benchmark report; the harness will annotate token counts so we can compute $/1M tokens for each variant.
[07:10] Lena: what about service level on p99? we need a plan if p99 is breached in production.
[07:15] Diego: Redwood supports graceful degradation: fallback model variants, region failover, and routing to burst capacity. for the POC we'll test fallback triggers and measure how traffic shifts.
[07:32] Marcus: let's talk numbers more concretely for our expected peak — 40 concurrent users, average 0.7 QPS per conversational session, peak 120 QPS.
[07:45] Diego: ok 120 QPS peak with 80-token outputs -> that's ~9.6k tokens/s generated at peak. we'll use that to size GPU cluster and see if single-node can handle or we need multi-node.
[08:05] Sara: action items recap: Lena to share prompt corpus and traffic profile; Sara/Diego to run 48-hour benchmark and share results; schedule follow-up.

[20:10] [mid-call, various timestamps skipped for brevity]
[20:12] Diego: note on instrumentation: we'll capture per-request TTFT, per-token time series, and have a synthetic trace view. we'll also record epoch-based cold-start counters to identify tail events. beware transcription: sometimes kv-cache is written as 'k v cache' in notes, but meaning remains.
[31:05] Marcus: curious about measurement noise — how do you control for infra jitter?
[31:12] Diego: we run multiple repetitions and use percentile aggregation across the full 48-hour window. we also record system metrics (CPU, GPU util%) and isolate noisy neighbors by pinning Dedicated pools.
[41:45] Lena: for acceptance criteria — can you provide a simple table in the report? e.g., pass/fail per metric with tolerances.
[41:52] Sara: yes, we'll produce a pass/fail sheet: e.g., TTFT p95 threshold, TTFT p99 threshold, TPOT p95 threshold, end-to-end p95 requirement, cost per 1M tokens. each will be green/amber/red with notes.
[45:00] Priya: do you have examples of prior POCs where p95 was < 200ms?
[45:06] Diego: we have internal benchmarks on smaller models hitting p95 TTFT ~150-200ms on dedicated with warm cache; larger models naturally higher. we'll include comparable runs in the appendix but note model architecture differences.
[50:30] Sara: ok next steps readout: Redwood will run initial small-run by 2027-07-09, full 48h benchmark by 2027-07-14, then we reconvene 2027-07-16 to review.
[50:50] Lena: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[51:00] Priya: thanks, talk soon.

Recap (auto):
- Defined TTFT vs TPOT and how they map to end-user response times.
- Agreed proposed POC success thresholds (TTFT p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms; TPOT p95 < 30ms; end-to-end p95 < 2.5s) as starting point.
- Redwood to run 48-hour benchmark that includes cold/warm/stress runs and provide pass/fail sheet + cost estimates.
